subject: Pilot surge + downgrade path for mixed-feature bundle
messages:
From: Olivia Parkol <olivia@caregrid.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging options for upcoming pilot — surge seats + downgrade

Hi Irene,

Hope you’re well. We’re getting ready to spin up a 6-week pilot across two product teams and expect a concentrated burst of inference traffic during launch windows. A few asks from procurement/engineering: 

- We want a short-term option that lets us burst to higher throughput without a long-term seat commitment.
- Ability to roll back to our baseline tier automatically at month-end (or earlier) with clear prorating.
- We use both chat and embeddings; ideally a single bundle that covers the feature set but with predictable unit economics.
- Procurement needs a pricing snapshot and a worksheet they can use to estimate monthly spend.

Can you outline packaging options and any one-time credits or pilot discounts you can offer? If there’s a simple downgrade path at month-end, that will make approvals much easier.

Thanks — Olivia
Olivia Parkol
Director, Product Operations
CareGrid Health

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Parkol <olivia@caregrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for upcoming pilot — surge seats + downgrade

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: yes, we can support a burst-first pilot with an explicit downgrade path and a single bundle that covers chat + embeddings. Details below and a suggested next step.

Quick proposal (pilot-friendly):
- Pilot bundle: "Pilot Surge Bundle" — includes chat (gen) + embeddings in a single SKU.
- Surge capacity: reserved burst seats (hourly-metered) that attach to your existing baseline capacity. Hourly metering prevents a full-month seat commitment.
- Price guardrails: prorated billing for surge hours; automatic step-down to baseline at the end of the pilot window (configurable, default: midnight of final day).
- Feature gating: enable chat+embeddings by default; optional add-on for deduped prefix caching (useful for prompt-heavy workflows) if you want lower unit cost during bursts.

We typically show two offers to speed procurement:
1) Soft pilot: 25% pilot discount on surge hours for first 30 days, no contract change required.
2) Enterprise pilot: 30% off first month + committed minimum of 6 months (convertible to Reserved/ Dedicated).

I’ll loop Ben for the exact pricing worksheet and a one-page MAP (mutual action plan) your procurement can use. If that looks good I can schedule a 30-min pricing workshop with procurement + eng next week.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of GTM — Mid Market
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Parkol <olivia@caregrid.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for upcoming pilot — surge seats + downgrade

Olivia — quick pricing grid to make this actionable for procurement. Attachment: pricing-grid.csv (stub) and redwood-surge-proposal.pdf (stub).

Summary options (per-hour equivalents shown for clarity):
- Baseline (current): 10 baseline seats, chat+embeddings enabled; $0.06 per 1k tokens gen, $0.002 per embedding unit.
- Hourly Surge Seats (pilot bundle): $1.75 per surge-seat-hour (metered). Pilot discount option A: 25% off surge-seat-hours for first 30 days -> $1.31/hr.
- Committed Surge Bucket (6-month): bulk price = $1.10 per surge-seat-hour (tiered), conversion credit applied if reserved after pilot.
- Proration: surge charges prorated to the hour; unused committed hours convertible to credits on 1:1 basis for the following 30 days.

Small concession we can make to accelerate approval:
- One-time $2,000 pilot credit applied on invoice if you sign a procurement acknowledgement within 10 business days.

Questions for you (to speed this along):
- Procurement contact (name + email) for PO routing?
- Are SOC2 + data-retention docs sufficient, or do you need an additional attestation for on-demand surge?

If you confirm procurement contact, I’ll produce a one-page MAP and a short SOW draft that describes the downgrade automation and how the step-down will be executed.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Peterson <sam.proc@caregrid.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Olivia Parkol <olivia@caregrid.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 09:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for upcoming pilot — surge seats + downgrade

Thanks Ben/Team. A few procurement notes — copying Olivia for context.

- We prefer not to commit to headcount-based seats for pilots. Hourly surge-metering is OK provided it caps at a pre-agreed monthly not-to-exceed (NTE) amount. Can you add an NTE cap to the pilot plan?
- PO process: we need a line-item price and a sample invoice layout. Please include the $2,000 pilot credit as a line item.
- Security: SOC2 Type II is sufficient, but we also need confirmation that logs for surge events can be routed to our audit bucket for 30 days.
- Downgrade: we need a documented rollback plan that shows exactly how feature toggles will be disabled and that we can request immediate step-down via API.

If you can get a MAP + SOW and the hourly NTE cap language, we can route this through procurement this week.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Peterson
Senior Procurement Manager
CareGrid Health

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Parkol <olivia@caregrid.com>, Sam Peterson <sam.proc@caregrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 15:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for upcoming pilot — surge seats + downgrade

Sam / Olivia — thanks, good constraints. Actionable next steps from our side: 

1) I attached the MAP (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) and a short PDF proposal (redwood-surge-proposal.pdf) that includes an NTE cap clause example and sample invoice layout. Please review.
2) SOW: Ben — can you prepare a 1-page SOW that includes the NTE cap, prorated surge billing by the hour, the $2k pilot credit as a line item, and the API-based immediate-step-down call (we implement a POST /api/v1/admin/stepdown). Put a placeholder for SOC2 evidence and the audit-log export window (30 days).
3) Legal: CCing Marissa to review the NTE language and the API rollback clause. Marissa — short ask: can you confirm we’re comfortable exposing the immediate-step-down endpoint in the SOW and recommend any guardrails we should add?

If CareGrid signs the acknowledgement by next Wednesday we’ll apply the $2k credit and enable the pilot bundle in your account. I’ll schedule a 30-min workshop with eng/procurement for early next week to walk through invoicing and the rollback test.

Best,
Irene
Head of GTM — Mid Market
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood-surge-proposal.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx, pricing-grid.csv
